summary: Couch Investor's September 22 video presents three 'buy and forget' growth stocks, framed by his thesis that the hyperscaler capex wave is rational: trailing 3-year return on invested capital for Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle sits well above their weighted average cost of capital and is expected to improve. His first pick is Amazon (BUY): AWS is a $148.4B business growing 27.5% that he argues is worth $1T+ of Amazon's ~$2.7T market cap, leaving ~$700B of other revenue (advertising, subscriptions, retail) effectively on top; free cash flow is pressured now but projected to recover by 2028, with ~15.7% growth taking revenue over $1T in ~2.5 fiscal years. Second is Meta (BUY): up 36% in a month to $741 on Muse traction (outperforming ChatGPT's early adoption thanks to Meta's distribution), still undervalued per his DCF at above $800/share; he calls Amazon's move to block Muse from shopping on amazon.com an amateur mistake that will be reversed, praising Shopify's deep agentic-checkout partnership instead. Third is Nvidia (BUY): a $5.4T valuation but only 18.8x forward earnings and 0.5x PEG, with ~65% operating margins, cash from operations up from $5.6B to $134.3B in ~4 years, and expected revenue growth of ~90%/65% in FY27/FY28 — he finds it absurd the market pays AMD ~55x forward earnings (a $1T cap) while Nvidia gets no premium. He also mentions Alphabet, Microsoft, Oracle, AMD (owned since ~$80-110) and Broadcom, and says dips in these names are opportunities for long-term holders. Calls: AMZN BUY; META BUY; NVDA BUY.
title: 3 Growth Stocks to Buy and Forget (they win every time)
